root_cause.text: The bridge neighbor-suppression paths in `br_device.c` and `br_input.c` used `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` to decide whether to process IPv6 ND packets, which allowed `br_do_suppress_nd()` to run even when IPv6 was boot-disabled and `ipv6_stub->nd_tbl` was never initialized, leading to a NULL dereference in `neigh_lookup()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says that with `ipv6.disable=1`, `inet6_init()` exits before `ndisc_init()` initializes `nd_tbl`, and then an ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery packet hitting a bridge with `neigh_suppress` enabled makes `br_do_suppress_nd()` dereference `ipv6_stub->nd_tbl` which is NULL; the patch fixes this by replacing `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` with `ipv6_mod_enabled()` in the bridge callers, “disabling NS/NA suppression when IPv6 is disabled.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use runtime IPv6 availability checks in bridge TX neighbor suppression logic instead of compile-time configuration checks.
intent_record.what: In `br_dev_xmit()`, the IPv6 branch condition changed from `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` to `ipv6_mod_enabled()` while keeping the rest of the IPv6 protocol, neighbor suppression, and `pskb_may_pull()` checks unchanged.
intent_record.how: The bridge will now take the IPv6 proxy-suppression path only when IPv6 support is actually enabled at runtime, rather than merely when the kernel was built with IPv6 support. This prevents the code from assuming IPv6 handling is available when it may be disabled or unloaded, avoiding inappropriate IPv6 processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the runtime IPv6 enablement check before applying bridge IPv6 neighbor suppression handling.
intent_record.what: In br_handle_frame_finish(), the IPv6-related conditional was changed from checking IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) to calling ipv6_mod_enabled() before testing for ETH_P_IPV6 and neighbor suppression support.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the bridge code now gates the IPv6 suppression path on the IPv6 module actually being enabled/available, rather than only on compile-time configuration. This prevents the IPv6-specific handling from being entered when IPv6 support is not active as a module.
